children.text: Chapter 1
uśan ha vai vājaśravasaḥ sarvavedasaṃ dadau
children.translated_text: Indeed, desiring merit, <s>Vājaśravasa</s> gave away all that he possessed.

children.text: tasya ha naciketā nāma putra āsa ||
children.translated_text: He had a son named <s>Naciketas</s>.

children.text: taṃ ha kumāraṃ santaṃ dakṣiṇāsu nīyamānāsu śraddhāviveśa
children.translated_text: When the gifts were being led away, faith entered him, though he was still a boy.

children.text: so 'manyata ||
children.translated_text: He thought:

children.text: pītodakā jagdhatṛṇā dugdhadohā nirindriyāḥ
children.translated_text: They have drunk their water, eaten their grass, yielded their milk, and have lost their faculties.

children.text: anandā nāma te lokās tān sa gacchati tā dadat ||
children.translated_text: Joyless are the worlds to which the man goes who gives such cattle.

children.text: sa hovāca pitaraṃ tata kasmai māṃ dāsyasīti
children.translated_text: He said to his father, 'Father, to whom will you give me?'

children.text: dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyam
children.translated_text: A second time, and a third time, he asked.

children.text: taṃ hovāca mṛtyave tvā dadāmīti ||
children.translated_text: He said to him, 'I give you to Death.'

children.text: bahūnām emi prathamo bahūnām emi madhyamaḥ
children.translated_text: Among many I go as the first; among many I go as the middle one.

children.text: kiṃ svid yamasya kartavyaṃ yan mayādya kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: What task of <s>Yama</s> will there be, which he will accomplish through me today?

children.text: anupaśya yathā pūrve pratipaśya tathāpare
children.translated_text: Look back as those before us were; look forward likewise to those after us.

children.text: sasyam iva martyaḥ pacyate sasyam ivājāyate punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A mortal ripens like grain, and like grain he is born again.

children.text: vaiśvānaraḥ praviśati atithir brāhmaṇo gṛhān
children.translated_text: A Brahmin guest enters houses as the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> fire.

children.text: tasyaitāṃ śāntiṃ kurvanti hara vaivasvatodakam ||
children.translated_text: They perform this appeasement for him: bring water, O descendant of <s>Vivasvat</s>.

children.text: āśāpratīkṣe saṃgataṃ sūnṛtāṃ ca iṣṭāpūrte putrapaśūṃś ca sarvān
children.translated_text: Hope and expectation, good company and pleasant speech, sacrifice and public works, sons and cattle, all these

children.text: etad vṛṅkte puruṣasyālpamedhaso yasyānaśnan vasati brāhmaṇo gṛhe ||
children.translated_text: he takes away from the man of little understanding in whose house a Brahmin stays without eating.

children.text: tisro rātrīr yad avatsīr gṛhe me anaśnan brahmann atithir namasyaḥ
children.translated_text: Since you have stayed in my house for three nights without eating, O Brahmin, a guest worthy of reverence,

children.text: namas te 'stu brahman svasti me 'stu tasmāt prati trīn varān vṛṇīṣva ||
children.translated_text: reverence be to you, O Brahmin; may there be welfare for me. Therefore choose three boons in return.

children.text: śāntasaṅkalpaḥ sumanā yathā syād vītamanyur gautamo mābhi mṛtyo
children.translated_text: May <s>Gautama</s> be calm in intention, well-disposed, and free from anger toward me, O Death.

children.text: tvatprasṛṣṭaṃ mābhivadet pratīta etat trayāṇāṃ prathamaṃ varaṃ vṛṇe ||
children.translated_text: When released by you, may he speak to me with recognition and trust. This I choose as the first of the three boons.

children.text: yathā purastād bhavitā pratīta auddālakir āruṇir matprasṛṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: As before, <s>Auddālaki Āruṇi</s> will be trusting when released by me.

children.text: sukhaṃ rātrīḥ śayitā vītamanyus tvāṃ dadṛśivān mṛtyumukhāt pramuktam ||
children.translated_text: Free from anger, he will sleep happily through the nights, having seen you released from the mouth of Death.

children.text: svarge loke na bhayaṃ kiṃcanāsti na tatra tvaṃ na jarayā bibheti
children.translated_text: In the heavenly world there is no fear at all; you are not there, nor does one fear from old age.

children.text: ubhe tīrtvā aśanāyāpipāse śokātigo modate svargaloke ||
children.translated_text: Having crossed beyond both hunger and thirst, one goes beyond sorrow and rejoices in the heavenly world.

children.text: sa tvam agniṃ svargyam adhyeṣi mṛtyo prabrūhi taṃ śraddadhānāya mahyam
children.translated_text: You, O Death, know the fire that leads to heaven; explain it to me, who have faith.

children.text: svargalokā amṛtatvaṃ bhajanta etad dvitīyena vṛṇe vareṇa ||
children.translated_text: Those who dwell in the heavenly world share in immortality. This I choose as my second boon.

children.text: pra te bravīmi tad u me nibodha svargyam agniṃ naciketaḥ prajānan
children.translated_text: I shall explain it to you; learn it from me, O <s>Naciketas</s>, understanding the fire that leads to heaven.

children.text: anantalokāptim atho pratiṣṭhāṃ viddhi tvam etaṃ nihitaṃ guhāyām ||
children.translated_text: Know this fire as the attainment of endless worlds and as the foundation, hidden in the secret place.

children.text: lokādim agniṃ tam uvāca tasmai yā iṣṭakā yāvatīr vā yathā vā
children.translated_text: He told him of that fire, the beginning of the worlds: what bricks there are, how many, and in what manner.

children.text: sa cāpi tat pratyavadad yathoktam athāsya mṛtyuḥ punar āha tuṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And he repeated it back exactly as it had been taught; then Death, pleased with him, spoke again.

children.text: tam abravīt prīyamāṇo mahātmā varaṃ tavehādya dadāmi bhūyaḥ
children.translated_text: The great-souled one, rejoicing, said to him, 'Here today I give you another boon.

children.text: tavaiva nāmnā bhavitāyam agniḥ sṛṅkāṃ cemām anekarūpāṃ gṛhāṇa ||
children.translated_text: This fire shall be named after you, and take this many-formed necklace.'

children.text: triṇāciketas tribhir etya sandhiṃ trikarmakṛt tarati janmamṛtyū
children.translated_text: The one who has performed the <s>triṇāciketa</s>, having entered into union with the three and performing the three rites, crosses beyond birth and death.

children.text: brahmajajñaṃ devam īḍyaṃ viditvā nicāyyemāṃ śāntim atyantam eti ||
children.translated_text: Knowing the praiseworthy god born of <s>Brahman</s>, and realizing him, one reaches this ultimate peace.

children.text: triṇāciketas trayam etad viditvā ya evaṃ vidvāṃś cinute nāciketam
children.translated_text: The one who has performed the <s>triṇāciketa</s>, knowing this triad, whoever, knowing thus, piles up the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire,

children.text: sa mṛtyupāśān purataḥ praṇodya śokātigo modate svargaloke ||
children.translated_text: he drives away the snares of death before him and, beyond sorrow, rejoices in the heavenly world.

children.text: eṣa te 'gnir naciketaḥ svargyo yam avṛṇīthā dvitīyena vareṇa
children.translated_text: This, O <s>Naciketas</s>, is your fire that leads to heaven, which you chose with your second boon.

children.text: etam agniṃ tavaiva pravakṣyanti janāsas tṛtīyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva ||
children.translated_text: People will proclaim this fire as yours alone. Choose your third boon, O <s>Naciketas</s>.

children.text: yeyaṃ prete vicikitsā manuṣye astīty eke nāyam astīti caike
children.translated_text: This doubt exists about a person who has died: some say, 'He exists,' and others say, 'He does not exist.'

children.text: etad vidyām anuśiṣṭas tvayāhaṃ varāṇām eṣa varas tṛtīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Taught by you, I would know this. This is the third boon among the boons.

children.text: devair atrāpi vicikitsitaṃ purā na hi sujñeyam aṇur eṣa dharmaḥ
children.translated_text: Even the gods formerly had doubt about this; for this <s>dharma</s> (truth of the matter) is subtle and not easy to know.

children.text: anyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva mā moparotsīr ati mā sṛjainam ||
children.translated_text: Choose another boon, O <s>Naciketas</s>; do not press me. Release me from this one.

children.text: devair atrāpi vicikitsitaṃ kila tvaṃ ca mṛtyo yan na sujñeyam āttha
children.translated_text: Even the gods had doubt about this, you say, O Death, and you say it is not easy to know.

children.text: vaktā cāsya tvādṛg anyo na labhyo nānyo varas tulya etasya kaścit ||
children.translated_text: No other speaker of it can be found like you, and no other boon is equal to this one.

children.text: śatāyuṣaḥ putrapautrān vṛṇīṣva bahūn paśūn hastihiraṇyam aśvān
children.translated_text: Choose sons and grandsons living a hundred years, many cattle, elephants, gold, and horses.

children.text: bhūmer mahad āyatanaṃ vṛṇīṣva svayaṃ ca jīva śarado yāvad icchasi ||
children.translated_text: Choose a great expanse of land, and live yourself for as many autumns as you wish.

children.text: etat tulyaṃ yadi manyase varaṃ vṛṇīṣva vittaṃ cirajīvikāṃ ca
children.translated_text: If you think this an equal boon, choose wealth and long life.

children.text: mahābhūmau naciketas tvam edhi kāmānāṃ tvā kāmabhājaṃ karomi ||
children.translated_text: Become great upon the broad earth, O <s>Naciketas</s>; I shall make you the enjoyer of desires.

children.text: ye ye kāmā durlabhā martyaloke sarvān kāmāṃś chandataḥ prārthayasva
children.translated_text: Whatever desires are hard to obtain in the mortal world, ask freely for all those desires.

children.text: imā rāmāḥ sarathāḥ satūryā na hīdṛśā lambhanīyā manuṣyaiḥ
children.translated_text: Here are women with chariots and musical instruments; such as these are not to be obtained by human beings.

children.text: ābhir matprattābhiḥ paricārayasva naciketo maraṇaṃ mānuprākṣīḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let yourself be served by these, given by me, O <s>Naciketas</s>; do not ask about death.

children.text: śvobhāvā martyasya yad antakaitat sarvendriyāṇāṃ jarayanti tejaḥ
children.translated_text: Ephemeral are these things of a mortal, O Ender; they wear away the vigor of all the senses.

children.text: api sarvaṃ jīvitam alpam eva tavaiva vāhās tava nṛtyagīte ||
children.translated_text: Even an entire life is only brief. Yours alone be the chariots, yours the dance and song.

children.text: na vittena tarpaṇīyo manuṣyo lapsyāmahe vittam adrākṣma cet tvā
children.translated_text: A human being cannot be satisfied by wealth. We shall obtain wealth if we have seen you.

children.text: jīviṣyāmo yāvad īśiṣyasi tvaṃ varas tu me varaṇīyaḥ sa eva ||
children.translated_text: We shall live as long as you rule; but the boon to be chosen by me is that very one.

children.text: ajīryatām amṛtānām upetya jīryan martyaḥ kvadhaḥsthaḥ prajānan
children.translated_text: Having approached the undecaying immortals, what decaying mortal here below, understanding this,

children.text: abhidhyāyan varṇaratipramodān atidīrghe jīvite ko rameta ||
children.translated_text: and brooding on pleasures of beauty, delight, and joy, would take pleasure in an excessively long life?

children.text: yasminn idaṃ vicikitsanti mṛtyo yat sāmparāye mahati brūhi nas tat
children.translated_text: Tell us, O Death, that about which they have this doubt, what concerns the great hereafter.

children.text: yo 'yaṃ varo gūḍham anupraviṣṭo nānyaṃ tasmān naciketā vṛṇīte ||
children.translated_text: This boon that has entered into the hidden matter: <s>Naciketas</s> chooses no other than that.

children.text: Chapter 2
anyacchreyo 'nyad utaiva preyas te ubhe nānārthe puruṣaṃ sinītaḥ
children.translated_text: The good is one thing, and the pleasant is another; these two, having different aims, bind a person.

children.text: tayoḥ śreya ādadānasya sādhu bhavati hīyate 'rthād ya u preyo vṛṇīte ||
children.translated_text: For one who takes up the good, it is well; one who chooses the pleasant falls away from the true goal.

children.text: śreyaś ca preyaś ca manuṣyam etas tau samparītya vivinakti dhīraḥ
children.translated_text: The good and the pleasant approach a human being; the wise man, having considered them together, distinguishes between them.

children.text: śreyo hi dhīro 'bhi preyaso vṛṇīte preyo mando yogakṣemād vṛṇīte ||
children.translated_text: For the wise man chooses the good in preference to the pleasant; the dull man chooses the pleasant for the sake of acquisition and preservation.

children.text: sa tvaṃ priyān priyarūpāṃś ca kāmān abhidhyāyan naciketo 'tyasrākṣīḥ
children.translated_text: But you, <s>Naciketas</s>, having reflected on dear and pleasing desires, have let them go.

children.text: naitāṃ sṛṅkāṃ vittamayīm avāpto yasyāṃ majjanti bahavo manuṣyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: You did not accept this chain made of wealth, in which many human beings sink.

children.text: dūram ete viparīte viṣūcī avidyā yā ca vidyeti jñātā
children.translated_text: These two, known as <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), are far apart, opposite, and going in different directions.

children.text: vidyābhīpsinaṃ naciketasaṃ manye na tvā kāmā bahavo 'lolupanta ||
children.translated_text: I regard <s>Naciketas</s> as one who longs for <s>vidyā</s>; many desires did not make you greedy.

children.text: avidyāyām antare vartamānāḥ svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṃ manyamānāḥ
children.translated_text: Dwelling in the midst of ignorance, thinking themselves wise and learned,

children.text: dandramyamāṇāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: fools wander about unsteadily, like blind men led by a blind man.

children.text: na sāmparāyaḥ pratibhāti bālaṃ pramādyantaṃ vittamohena mūḍham
children.translated_text: The hereafter does not become clear to the childish man, heedless and deluded by the bewilderment of wealth.

children.text: ayaṃ loko nāsti para iti mānī punaḥ punar vaśam āpadyate me ||
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'This world exists, there is no other,' he comes under my power again and again.

children.text: śravaṇāyāpi bahubhir yo na labhyaḥ śṛṇvanto 'pi bahavo yaṃ na vidyuḥ
children.translated_text: He is not obtainable even for hearing by many; even when hearing, many do not know him.

children.text: āścaryo vaktā kuśalo 'sya labdhā āścaryo jñātā kuśalānuśiṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Wonderful is the speaker of him, and skilled is the one who obtains him; wonderful is the knower, instructed by one who is skilled.

children.text: na nareṇāvareṇa prokta eṣa suvijñeyo bahudhā cintyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: This one, when taught by an inferior man, is not easily understood, being thought of in many ways.

children.text: ananyaprokte gatir atra nāsty aṇīyān hy atarkyam aṇupramāṇāt ||
children.translated_text: When taught by one who is not other than him, there is no further course here; for he is subtler than what is subtle and beyond reasoning.

children.text: naiṣā tarkeṇa matir āpaneyā proktānyenaiva sujñānāya preṣṭha
children.translated_text: This understanding is not to be obtained by reasoning; when taught by another, dear one, it is for true knowledge.

children.text: yāṃ tvam āpaḥ satyadhṛtir batāsi tvādṛṅ no bhūyān naciketaḥ preṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: You have attained that understanding; indeed you are firm in truth. May we have an asker like you, dear <s>Naciketas</s>.

children.text: jānāmy ahaṃ śevadhir ity anityaṃ na hy adhruvaiḥ prāpyate hi dhruvaṃ tat
children.translated_text: I know that what is called treasure is impermanent; for that permanent reality is not obtained by impermanent things.

children.text: tato mayā nāciketaś cito 'gnir anityair dravyaiḥ prāptavān asmi nityam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire was piled by me with impermanent materials, and I have obtained the eternal.

children.text: kāmasya āptiṃ jagataḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ krator anantyam abhayasya pāram
children.translated_text: The fulfillment of desire, the foundation of the world, the endlessness of sacrifice, the far shore of fearlessness,

children.text: stomamahad urugāyaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhṛtyā dhīro naciketo 'tyasrākṣīḥ ||
children.translated_text: the great praise, the wide-ranging and firm foundation: seeing these, steadfastly, you, wise <s>Naciketas</s>, let them go.

children.text: taṃ durdarśaṃ gūḍham anupraviṣṭaṃ guhāhitaṃ gahvareṣṭhaṃ purāṇam
children.translated_text: That ancient one, hard to see, hidden, entered within, placed in the cave, dwelling in the depth,

children.text: adhyātmayogādhigamena devaṃ matvā dhīro harṣaśokau jahāti ||
children.translated_text: the wise man, having understood that deity through attainment by the yoga of the self, abandons joy and sorrow.

children.text: etacchrutvā samparigṛhya martyaḥ pravṛhya dharmyam aṇum etam āpya
children.translated_text: Having heard this, having fully grasped it, having extracted this subtle righteous reality, and having attained it, a mortal

children.text: sa modate modanīyaṃ hi labdhvā vivṛtaṃ sadma naciketasaṃ manye ||
children.translated_text: rejoices, for he has obtained what is worthy of rejoicing. I think the dwelling is open for <s>Naciketas</s>.

children.text: anyatra dharmād anyatrādharmād anyatrāsmāt kṛtākṛtāt
children.translated_text: Different from <s>dharma</s> (right order), different from <s>adharma</s> (wrong), different from this done and undone,

children.text: anyatra bhūtāc ca bhavyāc ca yat tat paśyasi tad vada ||
children.translated_text: different from what has been and what will be: tell me that which you see.

children.text: sarve vedā yat padam āmananti tapāṃsi sarvāṇi ca yad vadanti
children.translated_text: The state which all the Vedas proclaim, which all austerities declare,

children.text: yad icchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti tat te padaṃ saṃgraheṇa bravīmi ||
children.translated_text: desiring which people practice <s>brahmacarya</s> (sacred studentship), that state I shall tell you briefly.

children.text: om ity etat ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>om</s>.

children.text: etaddhy evākṣaraṃ brahma etaddhyevākṣaraṃ param
children.translated_text: For this very syllable is <s>brahman</s>; this very syllable is the supreme.

children.text: etaddhyevākṣaraṃ jñātvā yo yad icchati tasya tat ||
children.translated_text: Having known this very syllable, whatever one desires, that is his.

children.text: etad ālambanaṃ śreṣṭham etad ālambanaṃ param
children.translated_text: This support is the best; this support is the supreme.

children.text: etad ālambanaṃ jñātvā brahmaloke mahīyate ||
children.translated_text: Having known this support, one is magnified in the world of <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścin nāyaṃ kutaścin na babhūva kaścit
children.translated_text: The discerning self is not born, nor does it die; it has not come from anywhere, nor has anything become from it.

children.text: ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre ||
children.translated_text: Unborn, eternal, everlasting, ancient, this one is not killed when the body is killed.

children.text: hantā cen manyate hantuṃ hataś cen manyate hatam
children.translated_text: If the killer thinks to kill, and if the killed thinks himself killed,

children.text: ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate ||
children.translated_text: both of them do not understand: this one does not kill, nor is he killed.

children.text: aṇor aṇīyān mahato mahīyān ātmāsya jantor nihito guhāyām
children.translated_text: Smaller than the small, greater than the great, the <s>ātman</s> (self) of this creature is placed in the cave.

children.text: tam akratuḥ paśyati vītaśoko dhātuprasādān mahimānam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One without self-will sees, free from sorrow, the greatness of the self through the serenity of the faculties.

children.text: āsīno dūraṃ vrajati śayāno yāti sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: Sitting, he goes far; lying down, he goes everywhere.

children.text: kas taṃ madāmadaṃ devaṃ mad anyo jñātum arhati ||
children.translated_text: Who other than me is fit to know that deity who is both joyful and joyless?

children.text: aśarīraṃ śarīreṣu anavastheṣv avasthitam
children.translated_text: Bodiless among bodies, established among unstable things,

children.text: mahāntaṃ vibhum ātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati ||
children.translated_text: having understood the great, all-pervading <s>ātman</s>, the wise man does not grieve.

children.text: nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena
children.translated_text: This <s>ātman</s> is not obtained by recitation, nor by intelligence, nor by much learning.

children.text: yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām ||
children.translated_text: It is obtained by the one whom this very self chooses; to him this <s>ātman</s> reveals its own form.

children.text: nāvirato duścaritān nāśānto nāsamāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Not one who has not turned away from bad conduct, not one who is not peaceful, not one who is not concentrated,

children.text: nāśāntamānaso vāpi prajñānenainam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: nor even one whose mind is not calm, can attain this self by insight.

children.text: yasya brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca ubhe bhavata odanaḥ
children.translated_text: He for whom both <s>brahman</s> and <s>kṣatra</s> become food,

children.text: mṛtyur yasyopasecanaṃ ka itthā veda yatra saḥ ||
children.translated_text: and for whom death is the seasoning: who truly knows where he is?

children.text: Chapter 3
ṛtaṃ pibantau sukṛtasya loke guhāṃ praviṣṭau parame parārdhe
children.translated_text: The two who drink the truth in the world of good deeds, who have entered the cave in the highest supreme place,

children.text: chāyātapau brahmavido vadanti pañcāgnayo ye ca triṇāciketāḥ ||
children.translated_text: knowers of <s>brahman</s> call them shade and light, as do those of the five fires and those who perform the threefold <s>Nāciketa</s> rite.

children.text: yaḥ setur ījānānām akṣaraṃ brahma yat param
children.translated_text: May we be able to know the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire, which is the bridge for sacrificers, and the imperishable, supreme <s>brahman</s>,

children.text: abhayaṃ titīrṣatāṃ pāraṃ nāciketaṃ śakemahi ||
children.translated_text: the fearless far shore for those who wish to cross over.

children.text: ātmānaṃ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīraṃ ratham eva tu
children.translated_text: Know the self as the rider in the chariot, and the body as the chariot itself.

children.text: buddhiṃ tu sārathiṃ viddhi manaḥ pragraham eva ca ||
children.translated_text: Know the intellect as the charioteer, and the mind as the reins.

children.text: indriyāṇi hayān āhur viṣayāṃsteṣu gocarān
children.translated_text: They say the senses are the horses, and the sense-objects are their ranges.

children.text: ātmendriyamanoyuktaṃ bhoktety āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise say that the self, joined with the senses and the mind, is the enjoyer.

children.text: yas tv avijñānavān bhavaty ayuktena manasā sadā
children.translated_text: But the one who lacks understanding, always with an unyoked mind,

children.text: tasyendriyāṇy avaśyāni duṣṭāśvā iva sāratheḥ ||
children.translated_text: his senses are uncontrolled, like bad horses for a charioteer.

children.text: yas tu vijñānavān bhavati yuktena manasā sadā
children.translated_text: But the one who has understanding, always with a yoked mind,

children.text: tasyendriyāṇi vaśyāni sadaśvā iva sāratheḥ ||
children.translated_text: His senses are controllable, like good horses for a charioteer.

children.text: yas tv avijñānavān bhavaty amanaskaḥ sadāśuciḥ
children.translated_text: But one who lacks discernment, who is without a disciplined mind and is always impure,

children.text: na sa tat padam āpnoti saṃsāraṃ cādhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: does not attain that state, and reaches saṃsāra (the cycle of rebirth).

children.text: yas tu vijñānavān bhavati samanaskaḥ sadā śuciḥ
children.translated_text: But one who has discernment, who has a disciplined mind and is always pure,

children.text: sa tu tat padam āpnoti yasmād bhūyo na jāyate ||
children.translated_text: does attain that state, from which one is not born again.

children.text: vijñānasārathir yas tu manaḥpragrahavān naraḥ
children.translated_text: The person for whom discernment is the charioteer and the mind is the reins

children.text: so 'dhvanaḥ pāram āpnoti tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: reaches the end of the road, that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: indriyebhyaḥ parā hy arthā arthebhyaś ca paraṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: Higher than the senses are the objects; higher than the objects is the mind.

children.text: manasas tu parā buddhir buddher ātmā mahān paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Higher than the mind is the intellect; higher than the intellect is the great self.

children.text: mahataḥ param avyaktam avyaktāt puruṣaḥ paraḥ
children.translated_text: Higher than the great is the unmanifest; higher than the unmanifest is the puruṣa (spirit).

children.text: puruṣān na paraṃ kiṃcit sā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is nothing higher than the puruṣa. That is the limit; that is the highest goal.

children.text: eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍho 'tmā na prakāśate
children.translated_text: This ātman (self), hidden in all beings, does not shine forth openly,

children.text: dṛśyate tv agryayā buddhyā sūkṣmayā sūkṣmadarśibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: but it is seen by subtle seers through a sharp and subtle intellect.

children.text: yacched vāṅmanasī prājñas tad yacchej jñāna ātmani
children.translated_text: The wise person should restrain speech and mind; he should restrain that in the knowing self.

children.text: jñānam ātmani mahati niyacchet tad yacchecchānta ātmani ||
children.translated_text: He should restrain knowledge in the great self, and restrain that in the peaceful self.

children.text: uttiṣṭhata jāgrata prāpya varān nibodhata
children.translated_text: Arise, awake; having reached the excellent teachers, understand.

children.text: kṣurasya dhārā niśitā duratyayā durgaṃ pathas tat kavayo vadanti ||
children.translated_text: The poets say that the path is hard to cross, difficult as the sharp edge of a razor.

children.text: aśabdam asparśam arūpam avyayaṃ tathārasaṃ nityam agandhavacca yat
children.translated_text: That which is soundless, touchless, formless, undecaying, likewise tasteless, eternal, and scentless,

children.text: anādy anantaṃ mahataḥ paraṃ dhruvaṃ nicāyya tan mṛtyumukhāt pramucyate ||
children.translated_text: beginningless, endless, higher than the great, and firm: having discerned that, one is freed from the mouth of death.

children.text: nāciketam upākhyānaṃ mṛtyuproktaṃ sanātanam
children.translated_text: The ancient story of <s>Naciketas</s>, spoken by Death,

children.text: uktvā śrutvā ca medhāvī brahmaloke mahīyate ||
children.translated_text: when told and heard by an intelligent person, is glorified in the world of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ śrāvayed brahmasaṃsadi
children.translated_text: Whoever, purified, recites this supreme secret in an assembly of Brahmins,

children.text: prayataḥ śrāddhakāle vā tad ānantyāya kalpate
children.translated_text: or at the time of a śrāddha rite, it becomes fit for infinity.

children.text: tad ānantyāya kalpata iti ||
children.translated_text: It becomes fit for infinity. Thus.

children.text: Chapter 4
parāñci khāni vyatṛṇat svayaṃbhūs tasmāt parāṅ paśyati nāntarātman
children.translated_text: The Self-born pierced the openings outward; therefore one looks outward, not toward the inner self.

children.text: kaścid dhīraḥ pratyag ātmānam aikṣad āvṛttacakṣur amṛtatvam icchan ||
children.translated_text: Some wise person, desiring immortality, turned his eyes back and saw the inward ātman.

children.text: parācaḥ kāmān anuyanti bālās te mṛtyor yanti vitatasya pāśam
children.translated_text: The immature run after outward desires; they go into the widely spread snare of Death.

children.text: atha dhīrā amṛtatvaṃ viditvā dhruvam adhruveṣv iha na prārthayante ||
children.translated_text: But the wise, having known immortality, do not seek the permanent here among impermanent things.

children.text: yena rūpaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ śabdān sparśāṃśca maithunān
children.translated_text: That by which one knows form, taste, smell, sounds, touches, and sexual pleasures,

children.text: etenaiva vijānāti kim atra pariśiṣyate
children.translated_text: by that alone one knows; what remains here?

children.text: etad vai tat ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is That.

children.text: svapnāntaṃ jāgaritāntaṃ cobhau yenānupaśyati
children.translated_text: That by which one beholds both the state of dream and the state of waking,

children.text: mahāntaṃ vibhum ātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati ||
children.translated_text: having understood that great, all-pervading ātman, the wise person does not grieve.

children.text: ya imaṃ madhvadaṃ veda ātmānaṃ jīvam antikāt
children.translated_text: Whoever knows this honey-eater, the living ātman, from close at hand,

children.text: īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate
children.translated_text: the lord of what has been and what will be, does not shrink away from it thereafter.

children.text: etad vai tat ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is That.

children.text: yaḥ pūrvaṃ tapaso jātam adbhyaḥ pūrvam ajāyata
children.translated_text: He who was born first from tapas (creative heat), who came into being before the waters,

children.text: guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantaṃ yo bhūtebhir vyapaśyata
children.translated_text: who, entering the cave, remains there, and who looked out through beings,

children.text: etad vai tat ||
children.translated_text: this indeed is That.

children.text: yā prāṇena sambhavati aditir devatāmayī
children.translated_text: She who comes into being with prāṇa, <s>Aditi</s>, consisting of the deities,

children.text: guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantīṃ yā bhūtebhir vyajāyata
children.translated_text: who, entering the cave, remains there, and who was born through beings,

children.text: etad vai tat ||
children.translated_text: this indeed is That.

children.text: araṇyor nihito jātavedā garbha iva subhṛto garbhiṇībhiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Jātavedas</s>, placed in the two fire-sticks, is like an embryo well carried by pregnant women.

children.text: dive diva īḍyo jāgṛvadbhir haviṣmadbhir manuṣyebhir agniḥ
children.translated_text: Day by day, Agni is to be praised by wakeful human beings who possess oblations;

children.text: etad vai tat ||
children.translated_text: this indeed is That.

children.text: yataś codeti sūryo astaṃ yatra ca gacchati
children.translated_text: That from which the sun rises and into which it sets,

children.text: taṃ devāḥ sarve arpitās tad u nātyeti kaścana
children.translated_text: in that all the gods are fixed; no one at all passes beyond it.

children.text: etad vai tat ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is That.

children.text: yad eveha tad amutra yad amutra tad anv iha
children.translated_text: What is here is there; what is there is likewise here.

children.text: mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyum āpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati ||
children.translated_text: He goes from death to death who sees here as if there were plurality.

children.text: manasaivedam āptavyaṃ neha nānāsti kiṃcana
children.translated_text: This is to be attained by the mind alone; here there is no plurality at all.

children.text: mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyuṃ gacchati ya iha nāneva paśyati ||
children.translated_text: He goes from death to death who sees here as if there were plurality.

children.text: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo madhya ātmani tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: The puruṣa, the size of a thumb, stands in the middle of the self,

children.text: īśāno bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate
children.translated_text: lord of what has been and what will be; thereafter one does not shrink away from him.

children.text: etad vai tat ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is That.

children.text: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo jyotir iva adhūmakaḥ
children.translated_text: The puruṣa, the size of a thumb, is like a smokeless light,

children.text: īśāno bhūtabhavyasya sa evādya sa u śvaḥ
children.translated_text: lord of what has been and what will be; he alone is today, and he indeed is tomorrow.

children.text: etad vai tat ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is That.

children.text: yathodakaṃ durge vṛṣṭaṃ parvateṣu vidhāvati
children.translated_text: As water rained upon a difficult height runs down among the mountains,

children.text: evaṃ dharmān pṛthak paśyaṃs tān evānu vidhāvati ||
children.translated_text: so one who sees dharmas (realities) as separate runs after those very things.

children.text: yathodakaṃ śuddhe śuddham āsiktaṃ tādṛg eva bhavati
children.translated_text: As pure water poured into pure water becomes just the same,

children.text: evaṃ muner vijānata ātmā bhavati gautama ||
children.translated_text: so, O <s>Gautama</s>, becomes the ātman of the sage who understands.

children.text: Chapter 5
puram ekādaśadvāram ajasyāvakracetasaḥ
children.translated_text: The city of eleven gates belongs to the unborn one whose consciousness is not crooked.

children.text: anuṣṭhāya na śocati vimuktaś ca vimucyate
children.translated_text: Having contemplated it, one does not grieve; freed, one is liberated.

children.text: etad vai tat ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is That.

children.text: haṃsaḥ śuciṣad vasur antarikṣasad dhotā vediṣad atithir duroṇasat
children.translated_text: The swan abiding in purity, the Vasu abiding in the midspace, the Hotṛ abiding at the altar, the guest abiding in the house,

children.text: nṛṣad varasad ṛtasad vyomasad abjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtaṃ bṛhat ||
children.translated_text: abiding among people, abiding in the excellent place, abiding in ṛta (cosmic order), abiding in space, born from water, born from cattle, born from ṛta, born from the mountain: the great ṛta.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ prāṇam unnayati apānaṃ pratyag asyati
children.translated_text: He leads prāṇa upward and casts apāna back inward.

children.text: madhye vāmanam āsīnaṃ viśve devā upāsate ||
children.translated_text: All the gods worship the dwarf seated in the middle.

children.text: asya visraṃsamānasya śarīrasthasya dehinaḥ
children.translated_text: When this embodied one, dwelling in the body, is being loosened,

children.text: dehād vimucyamānasya kim atra pariśiṣyate
children.translated_text: when he is being released from the body, what remains here?

children.text: etad vai tat ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is That.

children.text: na prāṇena nāpānena martyo jīvati kaścana
children.translated_text: No mortal at all lives by prāṇa or by apāna,

children.text: itareṇa tu jīvanti yasminn etāv upāśritau ||
children.translated_text: but they live by another, on which these two depend.

children.text: hanta ta idaṃ pravakṣyāmi guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam
children.translated_text: Come, I shall tell you this secret, the ancient <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: yathā ca maraṇaṃ prāpya ātmā bhavati gautama ||
children.translated_text: and how, having reached death, the ātman becomes, O <s>Gautama</s>.

children.text: yonim anye prapadyante śarīratvāya dehinaḥ
children.translated_text: Some embodied beings enter a womb in order to take bodily form;

children.text: sthāṇum anye 'nusaṃyanti yathākarma yathāśrutam ||
children.translated_text: others go into a stationary state, according to their karma and according to their knowledge.

children.text: ya eṣa supteṣu jāgarti kāmaṃ kāmaṃ puruṣo nirmimāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: This puruṣa who wakes among those who sleep, fashioning desire after desire,

children.text: tad eva śukraṃ tad brahma tad evāmṛtam ucyate
children.translated_text: That very thing is the bright one; that is <s>Brahman</s>; that alone is called immortal.

children.text: tasmiṃl lokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tad u nātyeti kaścana
children.translated_text: In it all worlds are established; no one at all goes beyond it.

children.text: etad vai tat ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is that.

children.text: agnir yathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva
children.translated_text: As the one fire, having entered the world, became corresponding in form to each form,

children.text: ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiś ca ||
children.translated_text: so the one inner self of all beings is corresponding in form to each form, and yet is outside them.

children.text: vāyur yathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva
children.translated_text: As the one wind, having entered the world, became corresponding in form to each form,

children.text: ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiś ca ||
children.translated_text: so the one inner self of all beings is corresponding in form to each form, and yet is outside them.

children.text: sūryo yathā sarvalokasya cakṣur na lipyate cākṣuṣair bāhyadoṣaiḥ
children.translated_text: As the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not stained by external defects belonging to sight,

children.text: ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā na lipyate lokaduḥkhena bāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so the one inner self of all beings is not stained by the suffering of the world, being outside it.

children.text: eko vaśī sarvabhūtāntarātmā ekaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti
children.translated_text: The one ruler, the inner self of all beings, who makes one form manifold,

children.text: tam ātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrās teṣāṃ sukhaṃ śāśvataṃ netareṣām ||
children.translated_text: the wise who behold him established in the self have eternal happiness, not others.

children.text: nityo 'nityānāṃ cetanaś cetanānām eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān
children.translated_text: The eternal among the non-eternal, the conscious among the conscious, the one who apportions desires to the many,

children.text: tam ātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrās teṣāṃ śāntiḥ śāśvatī netareṣām ||
children.translated_text: the wise who behold him established in the self have eternal peace, not others.

children.text: tad etad iti manyante 'nirdeśyaṃ paramaṃ sukham
children.translated_text: They think, 'This is that,' the indefinable supreme happiness.

children.text: kathaṃ nu tad vijānīyāṃ kim u bhāti vibhāti vā ||
children.translated_text: How indeed shall I know it? Does it shine, or does it shine forth?

children.text: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto 'yam agniḥ
children.translated_text: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars; these lightnings do not shine, much less this fire.

children.text: tam eva bhāntam anu bhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti ||
children.translated_text: When that alone shines, everything shines after it; by its light all this shines forth.

children.text: Chapter 6
ūrdhvamūlo avākśākha eṣo 'śvatthaḥ sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: This is the eternal <s>aśvattha</s> tree, with its root above and branches downward.

children.text: tad eva śukraṃ tad brahma tad evāmṛtam ucyate
children.translated_text: That very thing is the bright one; that is <s>Brahman</s>; that alone is called immortal.

children.text: tasmiṃllokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tad u nātyeti kaścana
children.translated_text: In it all worlds are established; no one at all goes beyond it.

children.text: etad vai tat ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is that.

children.text: yad idaṃ kiṃca jagat sarvaṃ prāṇa ejati niḥsṛtam
children.translated_text: Whatever there is, this whole moving world, has come forth and trembles in <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath).

children.text: mahad bhayaṃ vajram udyataṃ ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: It is a great terror, an uplifted thunderbolt; those who know this become immortal.

children.text: bhayād asyāgnis tapati bhayāt tapati sūryaḥ
children.translated_text: From fear of it fire burns; from fear the sun gives heat.

children.text: bhayād indraś ca vāyuś ca mṛtyur dhāvati pañcamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From fear both <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, and Death as the fifth, run on.

children.text: iha ced aśakad boddhuṃ prākśarīrasya visrasaḥ
children.translated_text: If one is able to understand it here before the body's dissolution,

children.text: tataḥ sargeṣu lokeṣu śarīratvāya kalpate ||
children.translated_text: then one is fitted for embodiment among created worlds.

children.text: yathādarśe tathātmani yathā svapne tathā pitṛloke
children.translated_text: As in a mirror, so in the self; as in a dream, so in the world of the fathers.

children.text: yathāpsu parīva dadṛśe tathā gandharvaloke chāyātapayor iva brahmaloke ||
children.translated_text: As it is seen, as it were, in water, so in the world of the <s>Gandharvas</s>; as light and shade, so in the world of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ pṛthagbhāvam udayāstamayau ca yat
children.translated_text: Having understood the separate nature of the senses, and their arising and setting,

children.text: pṛthag utpadyamānānāṃ matvā dhīro na śocati ||
children.translated_text: and that they are produced separately, the wise one does not grieve.

children.text: indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ mano manasaḥ sattvam uttamam
children.translated_text: Beyond the senses is the mind; higher than the mind is <s>sattva</s> (intelligence).

children.text: sattvād adhi mahānātmā mahato 'vyaktam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: Above <s>sattva</s> is the great self; higher than the great is the unmanifest.

children.text: avyaktāt tu paraḥ puruṣo vyāpako 'liṅga eva ca
children.translated_text: But beyond the unmanifest is the <s>puruṣa</s> (person), all-pervading and without mark.

children.text: yaṃ jñātvā mucyate jantur amṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati ||
children.translated_text: Knowing him, a creature is released and goes to immortality.

children.text: na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpam asya na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścanainam
children.translated_text: His form does not stand within sight; no one sees him with the eye.

children.text: hṛdā manīṣā manasābhikﾱpto ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: He is apprehended by the heart, by insight, and by the mind; those who know this become immortal.

children.text: yadā pañcāvatiṣṭhante jñānāni manasā saha
children.translated_text: When the five knowledges, together with the mind, come to rest,

children.text: buddhiś ca na viceṣṭati tām āhuḥ paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: and the intellect does not stir, they call that the highest course.

children.text: tāṃ yogam iti manyante sthirām indriyadhāraṇām
children.translated_text: They regard that as yoga: the firm holding of the senses.

children.text: apramattas tadā bhavati yogo hi prabhavāpyayau ||
children.translated_text: Then one becomes undistracted, for yoga has both arising and passing away.

children.text: naiva vācā na manasā prāptuṃ śakyo na cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: It cannot be attained by speech, nor by mind, nor by the eye.

children.text: astīti bruvato 'nyatra kathaṃ tad upalabhyate ||
children.translated_text: How can it be apprehended except by one who says, 'It is'?

children.text: astīty evopalabdhavyas tattvabhāvena cobhayoḥ
children.translated_text: It must be apprehended precisely as 'it is,' and also in its real nature, in both ways.

children.text: astīty evopalabdhasya tattvabhāvaḥ prasīdati ||
children.translated_text: For one by whom it has been apprehended precisely as 'it is,' its real nature becomes clear.

children.text: yadā sarve pramucyante kāmā ye 'sya hṛdi śritāḥ
children.translated_text: When all desires that are lodged in his heart are released,

children.text: atha martyo 'mṛto bhavaty atra brahma samaśnute ||
children.translated_text: then the mortal becomes immortal; here he attains <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: yadā sarve prabhidyante hṛdayasyeha granthayaḥ
children.translated_text: When all the knots of the heart are cut apart here,

children.text: atha martyo 'mṛto bhavaty etāvaddhyanuśāsanam ||
children.translated_text: then the mortal becomes immortal. This much is the instruction.

children.text: śataṃ caikā ca hṛdayasya nāḍyas tāsāṃ mūrdhānam abhiniḥsṛtaikā
children.translated_text: There are a hundred and one channels of the heart; of them one goes out through the crown of the head.

children.text: tayordhvam āyann amṛtatvam eti viṣvaṅṅ anyā utkramaṇe bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Going upward by that, one reaches immortality; the others, in every direction, serve for departure.

children.text: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo 'ntarātmā sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>puruṣa</s> (person), the inner self, the size of a thumb, is always seated in the hearts of people.

children.text: taṃ svāccharīrāt pravṛhen muñjād iveṣīkāṃ dhairyeṇa
children.translated_text: One should draw him out from one's own body with firmness, as the pith from a reed.

children.text: taṃ vidyācchukram amṛtaṃ taṃ vidyācchukram amṛtam iti ||
children.translated_text: One should know him as bright and immortal; one should know him as bright and immortal.

children.text: mṛtyuproktāṃ naciketo 'tha labdhvā vidyām etāṃ yogavidhiṃ ca kṛtsnam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Naciketas</s>, having received this knowledge taught by Death and the whole discipline of yoga,

children.text: brahmaprāpto virajo 'bhūd vimṛtyur anyo 'py evaṃ yo vid adhyātmam eva ||
children.translated_text: attained <s>Brahman</s>, became stainless and free from death; so also does another who knows thus concerning the self.
